integration_questions: With body_length 0.10 m, does the slalom progress move past the 0.17 to 0.18 plateau? If not, the stall is controller reaction time, not inertia.
Does steering_oscillation on the oval stay near 0.3 or below, or does the lower yaw inertia add jitter?
Does s-bend progress hold at or above 0.6? If it drops, the longer body was giving useful stability and body_length should return to 0.14 m.
Do line_loss_events stay near 1 per run at bend entries, and does control_effort stay near 5 to 9?

intent: Test whether cutting yaw inertia by shortening the body (body_length 0.14 to 0.10 m) lifts the slalom plateau without losing the s-bend or oval gains from iteration 8. Mass returns to 0.6 kg, since 0.5 kg was worse. All sensing and wheel values stay at the iteration 8 best. Expected: slalom progress above 0.2, s-bend progress at or above 0.6, oval at 18 or more of 20 finishes, and a score above 417.9.
learning: Iteration 9 showed that mass 0.5 kg hurt the oval and s-bend, so 0.6 kg stays. The slalom plateau has resisted every sensing and turn-rate lever, so the next test is yaw inertia through body_length, which is the only inertia term not yet tried. If body_length 0.10 m lifts the slalom or s-bend without adding oval oscillation, keep it and check whether wheel_radius can rise further. If it adds oscillation or lowers the s-bend, return to 0.14 m and report the slalom as a controller-side limit to the Integrator.
rationale: Iteration 9 (mass 0.5 kg) scored 382.3, below iteration 8 (417.9). The oval fell from 19/20 to 18/20 finishes, the s-bend progress dropped from 0.655 to 0.521, and the slalom stayed on its plateau (progress 0.165). So the lighter mass did not help, and I revert it to 0.6 kg. Across nine races the slalom has stalled at progress 0.16 to 0.18 under every change to sensing, footprint, track, radius, mass and row position. That points at the robot's turn response on the slalom's tight alternating bends, not at sensing. Yaw inertia is mass*(L^2+W^2)/12, so body_length is the one inertia lever I have not tested. Its only effect in the simulator is that inertia term, and it does not change the off-track limit. Reducing body_length from 0.14 m to 0.10 m (the allowed minimum) cuts the L^2+W^2 term from about 0.0340 to 0.0244, roughly 28 percent less yaw inertia at the same mass. I make this one change relative to iteration 8, keeping mass at 0.6 kg, so the effect is isolated. Expected result: faster yaw response, slalom progress above 0.2, and s-bend progress held near 0.65. The main risk is that a shorter body changes the sensor-to-axle relationship in a way the Integrator must check, or that the faster response adds oscillation on the oval, which already reads 0.31.
